steps.title: Connect a multi-cloud estate
steps.say: The simulated clouds start: six accounts on AWS, Azure and GCP with eight weeks behind them. Each is connected with a read-only role or identity reference; one connection that pastes an access key instead is refused and nothing is stored. Each connection backfills the account's inventory, hourly utilisation and daily CUR-style billing lines.

steps.title: Where the money goes
steps.say: Last week against the week before, split into what drove the change, and the inventory by cost. The most expensive resource is a Kubernetes node pool whose floor keeps nodes running all night that its demand does not need.

steps.title: Find idle and oversized spend
steps.say: The rightsizer forecasts every workload four weeks ahead and picks the smallest size whose p99 CPU stays under 80% and memory under 85% in 90% of sample paths; idle machines and unattached volumes are judged on the whole history. A change-risk model trained on the estate's own history sends risky changes to review. Beside it, the 14-day average-utilisation rule, and where the two disagree.

steps.title: A savings plan portfolio
steps.say: One-year commitments for the usage that will remain after rightsizing: a compute savings plan per cloud in $1-an-hour blocks and database reservations per instance type, chosen by a mixed-integer programme over twenty forecast scenarios of the next thirteen weeks. Against it, committing to last month's minimum, sized before any rightsizing.

steps.title: Simulate SLO risk
steps.say: Three plans run against 200 forecast sample paths of the next four weeks: the SLO-aware recommendations, the average-utilisation rule, and an aggressive rightsizer that aims at 95%. For each change, the probability that it breaks the SLO; for each plan, the savings and the breaches to expect.

steps.title: Terraform changes as a pull request
steps.say: The open recommendations become a Terraform diff per account repository and a pull request with the evidence, risk and rollback. Applying directly is refused by policy. The engineer who proposed it cannot approve it; the FinOps lead does, and the pull request is opened for the team's pipeline. The lead also approves the commitment portfolio. Nothing in any cloud has changed.

body.title: Rightsize idle and oversized resources (FinOps, October)

steps.title: Replay four weeks and verify
steps.say: The simulator is told that the team's pipeline merged and applied the pull request and that the commitments were bought, both the next morning; four weeks run and the connectors sync them. The savings verifier re-prices the old configurations against what the workloads actually did, through the commitments in force, and sets the before/after and list-price figures beside it; the simulation's true savings are shown for comparison. Then the week's bill against the week before the change, and the audit trail.
